title: test-0094-SOC-CIV-STATEGOVT
passage: In the recent state elections of Vidarbha, the political landscape shifted significantly. The state is divided into 288 distinct areas called constituencies, which are smaller than districts. Voters in each constituency cast their ballots to elect a single representative known as a Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA). Once the results were tallied, the party that secured more than half of the total seats—145 or more—was invited by the Governor to form the government. This majority rule ensures that the ruling party has the support of the people's representatives. After the party leader was chosen by the elected MLAs, the Governor officially appointed this person as the Chief Minister. It is important to note that the Chief Minister is not directly elected by the public, but is chosen by the MLAs who represent the people. While the Governor acts as the constitutional head of the state, they do not draft or pass laws. Instead, the Legislative Assembly, composed of all elected MLAs, is the body responsible for debating and passing state laws. The Governor’s role is primarily to ensure the government functions according to the constitution, rather than creating legislation.
summary: After the party leader was chosen by the elected MLAs, the Governor appointed the person as the Chief Minister. While the governor is the head of state, they don't make laws. Instead, the school is the body responsible for debating and passing state laws.
